turns.user: Explain why a lock prevents two writers from colliding.
turns.assistant:
I'll load your communication profile, then explain the lock behavior in that style.**Answer**
A `lock` (a turn-taking gate) lets only one writer change shared data at a time.

**Why**
Without a turn-taking gate, two writers can read and write the same data together.
Their changes can overwrite each other and leave broken results.
The gate forces each writer to wait until the other finishes.
So only one writer updates the data in any moment.

**Example**
Writer A takes the gate, updates a counter, then releases it.
Writer B waits, then takes the gate and updates the same counter safely.
